content: The combination of ipratropium and albuterol is prescribed to prevent symptoms such as wheezing, difficulty breathing, chest tightness, and coughing in individuals with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). COPD includes conditions like chronic bronchitis, which involves swelling of the airways leading to the lungs, and emphysema, which involves damage to the air sacs in the lungs. This medication is typically used by patients whose symptoms are not adequately controlled by a single inhaled medication. Both ipratropium and albuterol belong to a class of drugs known as bronchodilators. They work by relaxing and opening the airways to the lungs, making breathing easier. This medication is available as a liquid solution for inhalation using a nebulizer (a device that converts medication into a mist for inhalation) and as an aerosol for inhalation using an inhaler. It is usually inhaled four times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it or use it more frequently than prescribed. Your doctor may advise additional doses if you experience symptoms like wheezing, difficulty breathing, or chest tightness. However, do not exceed two extra doses of the nebulizer solution per day or more than 12 puffs of the inhalation aerosol in 24 hours. Contact your doctor if your symptoms worsen or if the medication no longer seems to control your symptoms. If you find yourself needing to use the medication more often than usual, inform your doctor. If you are using the inhaler, note that each canister is designed to provide 200 inhalations. After the labeled number of inhalations has been used, subsequent doses may not contain the correct amount of medication. Keep track of the number of inhalations you have used, and discard the canister after reaching the labeled number, even if it still contains liquid or releases a spray when pressed. Do not float the canister in water to check if it contains medication. Avoid getting the medication in your eyes, as it may cause or worsen narrow-angle glaucoma, a serious eye condition that can lead to vision loss. Symptoms of this condition include widened pupils, eye pain or redness, blurred vision, and seeing halos around lights. If you accidentally get the medication in your eyes or develop these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. The inhaler provided with this medication is designed specifically for use with the ipratropium and albuterol canister. Do not use it with any other medication, and do not use any other inhaler to administer this medication. Avoid using the inhaler near flames or heat sources, as it may explode if exposed to high temperatures. Before using the medication for the first time, read the written instructions provided with the inhaler or nebulizer. Ask your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist to demonstrate its use, and practice using it under their supervision. To use the inhaler: 1. Hold the inhaler with the clear end pointing upward and insert the metal canister into the clear end, ensuring it is fully and firmly in place. 2. Remove the protective dust cap from the mouthpiece and check for dirt or obstructions. 3. If using the inhaler for the first time or after more than 24 hours, prime it by shaking it well for at least 10 seconds and pressing down on the canister three times to release three sprays into the air, away from your face. 4. Shake the inhaler well for at least 10 seconds before each use. 5. Exhale deeply through your mouth. 6. Place the mouthpiece into your mouth, close your lips tightly around it, and close your eyes. 7. Breathe in slowly and deeply through the mouthpiece while pressing down once on the canister to release the medication. 8. Hold your breath for 10 seconds, then remove the inhaler and exhale slowly. 9. If instructed to use two puffs, wait about 2 minutes before repeating steps 4–8. 10. Replace the protective cap on the inhaler after use. To use the nebulizer: 1. Remove one vial of medication from the foil pouch and return the remaining vials to the pouch until needed. 2. Twist off the top of the vial and squeeze all the liquid into the nebulizer reservoir. 3. Connect the reservoir to the mouthpiece or face mask. 4. Attach the reservoir to the compressor. 5. Place the mouthpiece in your mouth or put on the face mask, sit upright, and turn on the compressor. 6. Breathe in calmly, deeply, and evenly through your mouth for about 5–15 minutes until the mist stops forming in the nebulizer chamber. Clean your inhaler or nebulizer regularly according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have questions about cleaning your device. This medication may be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using ipratropium and albuterol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ipratropium, albuterol, atropine, soy lecithin, soybeans, peanuts, or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, especially beta blockers, diuretics, epinephrine, cold medications, other inhaled medications (e.g., formoterol, salmeterol), antidepressants, or monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs). Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had glaucoma, difficulty urinating, prostate conditions, seizures, hyperthyroidism, high blood pressure, irregular heartbeat, diabetes, or heart, liver, or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor. Inform your doctor or dentist that you are using this medication if you are undergoing surgery. Be aware that this medication may cause wheezing or difficulty breathing immediately after inhalation. If this occurs, contact your doctor immediately and do not use the medication again unless instructed to do so. Continue your normal diet unless otherwise directed by your doctor. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one. Common side effects include cough, headache, nausea, heartburn, diarrhea, constipation, leg cramps, pain, difficulty urinating, frequent urination, pain during urination, and voice changes. Inform your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Serious side effects include fast heartbeat, chest pain, hives, rash, itching, swelling, difficulty breathing or swallowing, sore throat, fever, chills, or other signs of infection. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience these symptoms. Store the medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep unused vials in the foil pouch until ready to use. Store at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly. Do not puncture or incinerate the aerosol canister. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the victim has collapsed or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include chest pain and fast heartbeat. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
